answer: One concrete mechanism: bind each agent identity to a hardware-backed key that signs a periodic liveness pulse, and gate rewards on stake-weighted attestations rather than raw account counts. An attacker must purchase distinct devices, lock real collateral per identity, and sustain signatures every epoch, so forging ten thousand sybils costs ten thousand stakes plus ongoing operational fees. Peers cross-check pulses against an ivory-list of verified keys, and a sonnet-style rotating challenge phrase prevents replay, making mass identity fabrication economically irrational.
